messages:
amanda: Heads-up: PR for per-tenant token-aware hysteresis fallback landed. Looking for design feedback before I wire into router. TL;DR: prefer lower-cost model on transient cost/latency spikes unless quality regressions persist beyond a grace window. sketch + questions below.

jon: Can you paste the proto/config you had in mind? curious about the thresholds and cool-down semantics.

amanda: gist of config (proto-like):
```
fallback_policy: "hysteresis"
cost_bias: 0.7          # 0..1 favor cost vs quality
spike_window_ms: 5000   # short-term spike detector
cooldown_ms: 300000     # how long to stick to fallback
min_samples: 20         # require N samples before commit
affinity_migration: "graceful" # keep session pinned, warmup probe
```

priya: cost_bias is interesting. how do we estimate cost in real-time? token-estimate per request or observed token counts over window? also per-route vs global decision?

sree: we already emit token-metering in the console but per-request token-estimate needs to be fast and conservative. we can use token_est (cheap) + rolling observed counts to adjust bias.

jon: big tradeoff: picking the cheaper model may reduce quality. we need eval hooks + a rollback certificate (automated signal that forces immediate revert) if quality drops. also KV-cache migration when switching variants is a huge perf hit — cold-cache cost may outweigh savings.

amanda: agreed. plan: keep session affinity for X minutes so most sessions stick. on variant switch we do a warmup probe to prefill KV cache for that session. if warmup fails N times -> mark fallback as degraded and either revert or mark for ops review.

kai: what do you mean by warmup probe? we must avoid sending real user content to synthetic probes. use a small, non-sensitive warmup prompt set per-tenant (stored encrypted) that approximates typical token lengths.

lucas: ops-bot: created ticket INF-2023 for runbook + metrics contract (owners: amanda, sree, priya). link: https://redwood.atlassian/browse/INF-2023

deploy-bot: deploy queued: canary pipeline for branch per-tenant-hysteresis at commit abc123. Canary target: 5% tenants, prefixed test accounts only.

priya: observability must include these signals: per-tenant quality proxy (embed-sim or small eval set), latency p50/p95, token-cost delta, cache-hit ratio, and number of warmup probes. Without quality signal we can't safely bias to cost.

amanda: action items I will take: 1) RFC draft with proto + state machine + probe definition, 2) metric contract for console + alert thresholds, 3) rollback certificate format (signed assertion), 4) ops runbook + safe defaults. I'll drop RFC by EOD.

sree: +1 on RFC. also we should design the hysteresis controller to be stateless in the router and keep soft-state in a small per-tenant controller service (easier to snapshot/replay). :thumbsup:

jon: sgtm. meet 4pm to lock probe semantics. If we can get a small canary on non-prod tenants this week we can iterate fast.

amanda: thanks all — will post RFC link here when ready.
